default.aiSummary: Aditi has shipped 10 of the last 12 days on the Full Stack Web Dev track, including an accessible modal with proper focus-trapping and a client-side rate limiter built without libraries — both signal she reaches for the harder, more correct implementation rather than the shortcut. She missed Day 9 (infinite scroll) but recovered the next day, submitting Day 10 late rather than skipping it. Momentum is trending up: 8-day streak at its peak, current run of 2 after the miss.

newUser.name: Rohan Verma
recruiterSuggestions: Add a project link to your Day 1 LinkedIn post
Keep the streak going — Day 2 unlocks your next badge
newUser.aiSummary: Rohan just shipped Day 1 on the AI / ML Engineering track — a landing page for his model demo. One day in, momentum is building.

1.title: Build Your Dev Landing Page
1.description: Every builder needs a home base. Build a single-page personal site with your name, one-line bio, and links to GitHub + LinkedIn.
requirements: Includes your name and a short bio
1.caption: Shipped my first project of the challenge — a landing page I'm actually proud of.

2.title: Responsive Navbar Component
2.description: Build a reusable navbar component that collapses into a hamburger menu below 480px.
2.caption: Nailed the hamburger menu breakpoint on the third try.

3.title: Form Validation From Scratch
3.description: Build a signup form with client-side validation — no libraries. Handle empty fields, invalid email, and weak passwords.
3.caption: No libraries, just vanilla validation. Felt good to build it from scratch.

4.title: Fetch and Render an API
4.description: Pick any public API and render its data as cards, with loading and error states.
4.caption: First time handling a failed fetch gracefully instead of just console.logging it.

5.title: Dark Mode Toggle
5.description: Add a persistent dark mode toggle to any past project using CSS variables.
requirements: No flash of wrong theme on load
Meets contrast guidelines in both modes
5.caption: Dark mode with zero flash on load — harder than it looks.

6.title: Build a Kanban Board
6.description: Drag-and-drop task board with 3 columns: Todo, Doing, Done. Persist state locally.
6.caption: Drag-and-drop still feels like magic even after building it myself.

7.title: Authentication UI Flow
7.description: Build the UI (not backend) for login, signup, and forgot-password — including all error and loading states.
7.caption: Spent most of today on error states nobody will ever compliment me for.

8.title: Build a Markdown Previewer
8.description: Live markdown editor with a real-time rendered preview pane.
requirements: Supports headers, bold, links, code blocks
Works on mobile as stacked panes

9.title: Infinite Scroll Feed
9.description: Build a feed that loads more items as the user scrolls, without pagination buttons.
9.caption: Missed today — exam prep took over. Back tomorrow.

10.title: Accessible Modal Component
10.description: Build a modal that traps focus, closes on Escape, and restores focus to the trigger element on close.
requirements: Focus returns to trigger on close
10.caption: Focus trap finally clicked. Submitted a day late but didn't skip it.

11.title: Rate Limiter (Client-Side)
11.description: Implement a simple client-side rate limiter for a search input using debounce and throttle.
11.caption: Debounce vs throttle finally makes sense in my hands, not just in theory.

12.title: Build a Streak Tracker Widget
12.description: Build a small embeddable widget that visualizes a daily streak as a grid of filled/empty cells, similar to a GitHub contribution graph. It should take a simple array of booleans as input and render entirely client-side.
requirements: Renders a grid from an array of daily completion values
Distinct visual states for completed, missed, and today
No external charting library — build the grid yourself
12.caption: Today's build: turning my own streak into a widget.

13.title: Command Palette (Cmd+K)
13.description: Build a searchable command palette triggered by Cmd+K / Ctrl+K.

14.title: Optimistic UI Updates
14.description: Implement optimistic updates for a like/upvote button with rollback on failure.
